LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 14.3.1 SENTENCES: ACTIVE AND PASSIVE VOICE

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.3: Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should one use a variety of sentences?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify sentences in the active and passive voice
2. construct sentences in the active and passive voice
3. appreciate the use of active and passive voice in effective communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 14.3.1 SENTENCES: ACTIVE AND PASSIVE VOICE
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 14.3.1 SENTENCES: ACTIVE AND PASSIVE VOICE
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify sentences in the active and passive voice

What this means
In this part you learn to identify sentences in the active and passive voice. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify sentences in the active and passive voice.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify sentences in the active and passive voice. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Construct sentences in the active and passive voice

What this means
In this part you learn to construct sentences in the active and passive voice. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct sentences in the active and passive voice.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct sentences in the active and passive voice. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the use of active and passive voice in effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the use of active and passive voice in effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the use of active and passive voice in effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the use of active and passive voice in effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify sentences in the active and passive voice)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice to a partner. (skill: construct sentences in the active and passive voice)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the use of active and passive voice in effective communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify sentences in the active and passive voice.
3. Practise this skill: construct sentences in the active and passive voice.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the use of active and passive voice in effective communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should one use a variety of sentences?
2. How can one tell the doer and the receiver of an action in a sentence?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify sentences in the active and passive voice.
5. Be able to: construct sentences in the active and passive voice.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
